body:
> Suggesting an alternative where once the body element is seen this cannot be modified.

This is already implied as far as I read the current spec, by "Contexts in which this element can be used:" in [4.2.5 The meta element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-meta-element); i.e., `<meta>` outside of `<head>` is invalid if the `name` attribute is present. I'm impressed how well the spec is written.

Our intention is as [Tab explained](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1771#issuecomment-3806639752):
> (a) it can only be set by a parser-created <meta>, (b) it's set and frozen by the _first_ such <meta> the parser sees, and (c) if the parser closes the <head> without seeing the meta, it's frozen as not-set, imo.

I found the logic is similar to `content-security-policy` when I read Blink's implementation. It blocks `document.write()` as well, but unfortunately it's not in this spec so I can't use its definitions in this PR.

This is different, I mean that you can't apply it once the body is seen, even if it's inserted to the head

> 
> Our intention is as [Tab explained](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1771#issuecomment-3806639752):
> > (a) it can only be set by a parser-created <meta>, (b) it's set and frozen by the _first_ such <meta> the parser sees, and (c) if the parser closes the <head> without seeing the meta, it's frozen as not-set, imo.

For b and c, The best way to spec this I think is to have this as a tri state of sorts (true, false, uninitialized) and set it to false on some conditions (eg body insertion). Not sure if parser-inserted is that important given the other conditions or what the best way to spec it given document.write().

> 
> I found the logic is similar to `content-security-policy` when I read Blink's implementation. It blocks `document.write()` as well, but unfortunately it's not in this spec so I can't use its definitions in this PR.

Not sure that dynamic content security policy injection is an example we should be following.

body:
This claim in CSS does not hold with the current text in this PR:

> Once set to either true or false, the flag will not change its value again for the lifetime of the [Document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document).

In particular, the spec doesn't prevent rerunning these steps after the `body` element has been parsed, as script could remove the `body` element, then insert a `meta` element, then insert the `body` again.

If the intent is to freeze the policy when a `meta` element is found or when the `body` element is parsed, the value should be tri-state (undeclared, false, true), and only change once from undeclared to false or true, and the parser should set the value to false (if still undeclared) when inserting a `body` or `frameset` element. (Should this also happen in the XML parser case?)

The CSS spec should also be updated to let HTML cover this aspect, so that there aren't two conflicting definitions.

body:
https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#iframe-frame-sizing says

> Navigating the iframe’s document causes it to forget its [locked embedded ICB size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#locked-embedded-icb-size).

This should be formalized in HTML when and how this happens. In particular, if the old document's frame size is kept while the new document is loading, information can leak between origins. (The alloworigins list is a contract between embeddee and embedder, not between embeddee and a new document being navigated to.) The size must be reset before the new document has a chance to make detectable decisions based on the viewport size (for example loading an image from `<picture><source media=...>` or `srcset`/`sizes` in the preload scanner). (Or the new document has to act as if this has happened.)

  - This only works for the HTML parser case. The XML parser case needs to be defined separately (see https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#parsing-xhtml-documents ). Scripting case not covered.

I suspect the first option is simpler.
